title: Types of Level Transmitters: A Complete Guide
queries: types of level transmitter in instrumentation
text:
Types of Level Transmitters: Introduction
 In many industrial processes, knowing how much material is inside a tank or vessel is extremely important. Industries such as water treatment, chemical processing, food production, oil & gas, and power plants rely heavily on accurate level measurement to maintain safe and efficient operations.
 This is where level measurement transmitters play a key role.
 A level transmitter is an instrument that continuously measures the level of liquids or bulk solids inside a tank, silo, or container. The transmitter converts the measured level into an electrical signal, usually 4–20 mA , which is then sent to a control system such as a PLC or DCS for monitoring and control.
 Level transmitters can measure a wide variety of materials including:
 Liquids such as water, fuel, oil, and chemicals

 Viscous liquids like syrups or sludge

 Bulk solids such as grains, powders, or pellets

 Because of their versatility, level transmitters are widely used in industries such as material handling, food & beverage, chemical plants, water treatment facilities, and power generation.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Working Principle of Level Transmitters
 Level transmitters operate using different physical principles depending on the technology used. Some transmitters measure pressure, others use sound waves or electromagnetic signals to determine the level inside a tank.
 For example:
 Capacitance transmitters measure changes in electrical capacitance.

 Hydrostatic transmitters measure pressure caused by the weight of liquid.

 Ultrasonic transmitters calculate level by measuring the travel time of sound waves.

 Radar transmitters use microwave signals to detect the surface of the liquid.

 Despite using different technologies, most level measurement systems determine level using three basic physical principles.
 1. Weight of the Fluid
 The weight of the liquid inside a tank creates pressure at the bottom. By measuring this pressure, the level of the liquid can be calculated.
 This principle is used in hydrostatic and pressure-based level transmitters.
 2. Pressure Head of the Fluid
 The height of liquid above a measurement point produces pressure known as hydrostatic pressure . The greater the height of the liquid column, the greater the pressure.
 Hydrostatic level transmitters use this principle to determine liquid levels.
 3. Position of the Fluid Surface
 Some transmitters measure the distance between the sensor and the liquid surface. This distance is then converted into level measurement.
 This principle is used by ultrasonic, radar, and microwave level transmitters.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Direct vs Indirect Level Measurement
 Level measurement methods are generally classified into two categories.
 1. Direct Level Measurement
 Direct measurement involves physically observing or detecting the level position directly.
 Examples include:
 Sight glass indicators

 Float-based level indicators

 Dipsticks

 Direct methods are simple but usually suitable only for small tanks or manual monitoring.
 2. Indirect Level Measurement
 Indirect methods measure a physical property related to the level, such as pressure, capacitance, or wave reflection.
 Most modern transmitters use indirect methods because they:
 Provide continuous measurement

 Work in harsh industrial environments

 Can measure very high or very low levels

 Contact vs Non-Contact Level Measurement
 Another important classification is contact and non-contact measurement technologies.
 1. Contact Level Measurement
 In contact measurement, the sensor touches the liquid or material being measured.
 Examples include:
 Capacitance transmitters

 Hydrostatic transmitters

 Guided radar transmitters

 These sensors are generally accurate but may be affected by corrosion, temperature, or chemical reactions.
 2. Non-Contact Level Measurement
 Non-contact sensors measure the level without touching the material.
 Examples include:
 Ultrasonic transmitters

 Radar transmitters

 These instruments are ideal for aggressive chemicals, high temperatures, or hygienic processes.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Types of Level Transmitters
 There are several technologies used to measure level in industrial applications. Each type has its own working principle and is suitable for specific conditions.
 Below are some of the most commonly used level transmitters in process industries.
 1. Capacitance Level Transmitters
 Capacitance level transmitters work based on the capacitance principle.
 A capacitor consists of two conductive plates separated by a dielectric material. In this type of transmitter:
 The probe acts as one plate of the capacitor

 The tank wall or reference electrode acts as the second plate

 The liquid acts as the dielectric medium

 When the level of liquid rises, the dielectric constant between the plates changes. This causes a change in capacitance value, which the transmitter converts into a level signal.
 These transmitters are commonly used for:
 Liquids

 Slurries

 Bulk solids

 Powder storage silos

 2. Hydrostatic Level Transmitters
 Hydrostatic level transmitters measure level based on liquid pressure at the bottom of a tank.
 The pressure produced by a liquid column depends on:
 Density of the liquid

 Height of the liquid column

 Gravitational acceleration

 By measuring this pressure using a pressure sensor , the transmitter calculates the level.
 Hydrostatic transmitters are widely used for:
 Water tanks

 Wastewater treatment plants

 Open reservoirs

 Underground storage tanks

 
 
 
 
 
 
 3. Magnetic Float Level Transmitters
 Magnetic float level transmitters use a magnetic float that moves with the liquid level.
 The float moves up and down with the liquid level. As it moves, the magnetic field interacts with sensors mounted outside the measuring chamber.
 These sensors detect the float position and convert it into a continuous level signal.
 Magnetic level transmitters provide:
 Stable measurement

 Good accuracy
